title: Lehmann spectral / Hilbert representation of thermal Green functions
expression_sketch: G(k, z) = Integral(rho(k, x)/(-z + x), (x, -oo, oo))/(2*pi);  G_R(k, omega) = G(k, omega + I*eta)  with eta -> 0+;  G(k, omega_n) = G(k, I*omega_n)
latent_structure: A single Cauchy/Hilbert master object G(k,z) interpolates the Matsubara propagator (z = i omega_n) and the retarded propagator (z = omega + i eta, eta->0+). Spectral density rho is the jump. Not CSE of G_R vs G_M components.

function_domains.G: Hilbert transform of rho; meromorphic/holomorphic off the real spectral support
function_domains.G_R: retarded: poles and discontinuities in the lower half-plane
function_domains.G_A: advanced: poles and discontinuities in the upper half-plane

derived_conditions.statement: beta is a finite positive integration endpoint
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: source uses integrals from 0 to beta and Fourier factor 1/beta; T=0 is not this formula

why_not_cse_lgg: Three presentations (Matsubara, retarded, advanced) of one Hilbert transform. CSE sees different denominators -i omega_n + omega' vs -(omega+i eta)+omega'; it does not invent the master G(z). LGG does not unify half-plane evaluations.
proposer_leak_risk: Lehmann, retarded, Matsubara, Hilbert names are in the source. Hide gold wording 'master analytic object' / 'unify G_R and G_M'. Integral is not in PARSE_POLICY; this is a representation identity, not a closed elementary form.
notes: beta>0 is not written as an inequality; it is the length of the declared imaginary-time interval [0,beta]. Labeled DERIVED from that interval, not from physical folklore T>0. Spectral support of rho is not further restricted by the source (no extra pole-exclusion import).
